exercise: AICC Face Matching - CLIP feature extraction baseline
cell_or_location: cell 5, emb = model(**procc) after procc = processor(img)
what_user_was_trying: Loop over face-matching images, preprocess each PIL RGB image with CLIPProcessor, and get a CLIP embedding from CLIPModel.
real_cause: processor(img) was called without return_tensors="pt", so the processor returned Python lists. CLIP's vision model expected pixel_values to be a PyTorch tensor with shape [batch, channels, height, width], then failed when it tried to read pixel_values.shape. The full model call also was not the clean route for image-only embeddings.
user_diagnosis_steps: Inspected the traceback until the failing line inside CLIPVisionEmbeddings showed pixel_values.shape, then connected that to procc["pixel_values"] being a list instead of a tensor.
user_fix: Call processor(images=img, return_tensors="pt") and pass the result to model.get_image_features(**inputs). If using GPU, move both model and inputs to the same device before inference.
memory_rule: Before calling a PyTorch model, verify the model input contract: tensors, not lists; expected batch dimension; expected shape; same device as the model. For Hugging Face processors, use return_tensors="pt" when feeding a Torch model.
next_drill: For the next vision baseline, print type(inputs["pixel_values"]), inputs["pixel_values"].shape, and next(model.parameters()).device before the first model call.

exercise: AICC Face Matching - CLIP feature extraction baseline
cell_or_location: cell 5, input_ids = procc[0] after procc = processor(img, return_tensors="pt")
error_message: Indexing with integers is not available when using Python based feature extractors
what_user_was_trying: Inspect the processed CLIP input after fixing return_tensors="pt", then pass the processed image into the CLIP model.
real_cause: CLIPProcessor returns a BatchFeature object, which behaves like a dictionary with named fields such as pixel_values. It is not a list or tuple, so integer indexing with procc[0] is invalid. For image-only CLIP feature extraction, the useful field is procc["pixel_values"], and the clean model call is model.get_image_features(**procc), not the full CLIP forward path.
user_diagnosis_steps: Read the traceback at the notebook line input_ids = procc[0], then connected the error message to the printed processor output being a named BatchFeature rather than a positional sequence.
user_fix: Use named-key access to inspect inputs, for example procc["pixel_values"], and pass the whole BatchFeature to model.get_image_features(**procc) for image embeddings.
memory_rule: Hugging Face processor outputs are usually dict-like batches: inspect .keys() first, then access inputs by name. Do not guess positional indexes for model inputs.
next_drill: For the next processor/model pair, print inputs.keys() and each tensor shape before the first model call.

exercise: AICC Face Matching - CLIP feature extraction baseline
cell_or_location: cell 5, emb = model(**procc) after procc contains only pixel_values
what_user_was_trying: Extract image embeddings from face images using CLIP after preprocessing each PIL image with CLIPProcessor.
real_cause: The full CLIPModel forward pass is for image-text comparison, so it runs both the vision branch and the text branch. The image processor output only contained pixel_values, not text token IDs. When CLIP tried to run the text model, input_ids was None and it raised the error.
user_diagnosis_steps: Printed the processor output and saw it only had the key pixel_values. Then followed the traceback from model(**procc) into CLIPModel.forward, where it called get_text_features(input_ids=input_ids) and failed because input_ids was missing.
user_fix: For image-only embeddings, call model.get_image_features(**procc) instead of model(**procc). If comparing images to text, also create text inputs with processor(text=..., images=..., return_tensors="pt", padding=True) so input_ids exists.
memory_rule: CLIP has two input contracts: images use pixel_values; text uses input_ids. The full CLIP forward needs both for image-text logits, while get_image_features needs only images.
next_drill: Run one tiny CLIP probe: print image_inputs.keys(), then image_features.shape from get_image_features; separately print text_inputs.keys(), then text_features.shape from get_text_features.
